name: Client Onboarding Sequence

parameters.content:
## Client Onboarding Sequence

### How it works

1. A scheduled trigger initiates the workflow to check client onboarding progression.
2. It fetches firm users and open matters from Clio, then processes and filters these matters based on client email and open date.
3. The workflow computes the onboarding stage by calculating days since matter opening and filters stages due today.
4. If a matter has a stage due, it builds an onboarding email, checks compliance via a sub-workflow, and verifies approval before sending.
5. Emails are sent out to clients with onboarding stages due, while those who opt out or have no stages due are skipped.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure Clio API credentials and set the CLIO_BASE_URL variable.
- [ ] Set up email sending credentials for the emailSend node.
- [ ] Configure the compliance check sub-workflow and ensure it is accessible.
- [ ] Adjust the schedule trigger timing as needed for onboarding checks.

### Customization

Customize the onboarding stages and email content in the 'Build Onboarding Stage Email' node to match your firm's client communication style.

## Trigger and data fetching

Starts the workflow on a schedule and fetches firm users and open matters data from Clio API.

## Process and filter matters

Splits open matters records, filters them by client email and open date, and calculates the onboarding stage based on days open.

## Identify stages due today

Filters matters with stages due today and checks if any stage exists to proceed further.

## Onboarding stage decision branch

Conditional decision to build onboarding email if a stage is due or skip otherwise.

## Compliance check and email sending

Runs compliance sub-workflow, checks approval, sends onboarding emails or skips if client opted out.

nodes.name: Every Day at 9am Trigger
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 9am (n8n server timezone). Feeds 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio' first, which passes straight through into 'Fetch Open Matters From Clio' — a genuine sequential dependency, not a disconnected side-fetch (see that node's notes for why this matters). Every open matter is re-checked on every run — there's no separate list of 'already sent' to maintain, because each matter's own open date tells this workflow exactly which stage (if any) is due today.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users from Clio API
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory once per run — used by 'Build Onboarding Stage Email' to resolve a matter's responsible_attorney id to a real name and email, so the welcome sequence can say 'your attorney, Jane Smith' instead of staying generic. Requesting 'email' works here because /users.json is the primary resource, not a nested association — same pattern PAC-63 uses for the same reason.

This node's single output item is passed straight through into 'Fetch Open Matters From Clio' unchanged (that node makes its own independent API call and ignores the incoming item's content) — the point of wiring it in series like this, rather than as a disconnected side-fetch referenced only by name, is that n8n only reliably executes a node during every run and every testing method (full run, single-node 'Execute step', etc.) when it's a genuine upstream dependency via an actual connection. A node with an incoming connection but no outgoing one is not guaranteed to run — this was confirmed the hard way live: 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio' as a disconnected parallel branch intermittently failed to execute even on full workflow runs, and consistently failed on single-node tests, causing 'Build Onboarding Stage Email' to error with "Node 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio' hasn't been executed."

Same Clio OAuth2 credential as the matters fetch — no separate setup. If this fetch fails, every matter's attorney simply fails to resolve and the emails fall back to generic firm contact details — it never blocks a send.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Matters from Clio API
nodes.notes:
Pulls every open matter — the next few nodes split, filter, and stage it. Runs after 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio' in sequence (see that node's notes for why), but makes its own independent API call and doesn't use anything from the incoming item. Same matters.json endpoint and 'status=Open' value as the New Matter Setup Bot (PAC-59).

'primary_email_address' as the nested field for a matter's client is the field name this catalog's Review Request Engine (NTC-17) already uses for Clio contact payloads elsewhere — reused here on the assumption Contacts (unlike Users) expose email through nested field selection, which PAC-63 confirmed live is NOT true for Users on tasks.json. Only 'responsible_attorney{id,name}' is requested here (no 'email') for exactly that reason — email is resolved afterward by matching the id against 'Fetch Firm Users From Clio'. Neither 'primary_email_address' on this specific endpoint nor 'responsible_attorney' itself as a field name has been independently confirmed live — check your first real run's output and adjust if Clio rejects either or returns something else.

'Never Error' is on, and downstream filtering treats a missing/empty 'data' array the same as zero matters — a Clio outage degrades this to a quiet skip rather than failing the run.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61/63 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Split Out Matter Records
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per matter, so the Filter and Code nodes downstream can each operate on individual matters. An empty or missing 'data' array (e.g. after a Clio error) simply produces zero items.

nodes.name: Filter Matters with Email and Date
nodes.notes: Drops matters with no client email on file, or no open date — there's nobody to email, or no date to compute a stage from. A nonzero drop rate here is worth checking in Clio periodically.

nodes.name: Calculate Days Since Open Date
nodes.notes: Runs once per matter (mode: Run Once for Each Item). Every matter gets a 'stage' field — empty string if today isn't one of its four sequence days — which the next node filters on. attorney_id is carried through unresolved; the build step further downstream is what turns it into a name and email.

nodes.name: Filter Matters Due for Stage Today
nodes.notes: Drops any matter whose days-since-open didn't land on exactly 0, 1, 3, or 7 — the vast majority of open matters on any given day. Only matters actually due for a sequence email survive to the next step.

nodes.name: Check If Stages Are Due Today
nodes.notes: Run Once for All Items (the default) — needs to see whether anything survived the filters above, not one matter at a time.

nodes.name: If Onboarding Stage Is Due
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one matter hit a sequence day today) → build and send.
No (nothing due — most days, for most firms) → route to Skip. No email sent.

nodes.name: Skip No Stage Due Today
nodes.notes: No open matter hit one of the four sequence days today. Expected on most days — this is normal, not a failure.

nodes.name: Build Onboarding Stage Email Content
nodes.notes:
Do not add an opt-out footer here — the compliance guardrail (next node) appends it automatically and logs the send attempt.

FIRM_CLIENT_PORTAL_URL is optional — copy adapts gracefully if unset (no dead link, no broken sentence). FIRM_ONBOARDING_CHECKLIST is a newline-separated list of items; leave unset for a sensible generic default. Personalization (attorney name/email) degrades gracefully to generic firm contact details if the attorney can't be resolved.

nodes.name: Execute Compliance Check Workflow
nodes.notes:
Checks whether this client has opted out of firm emails. If not, appends the required unsubscribe footer and logs the send attempt to the audit sheet — same pattern as the Invoice Reminder Ladder (PAC-18), since this is a genuine client-facing message, unlike PAC-61/63's internal-only notifications.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

Returns: { approved, message_out, recipient, suppression_reason } plus all upstream fields.

nodes.name: If Onboarding Email Approved
nodes.notes:
Yes (client hasn't opted out) → send.
No (client has opted out of firm emails) → route to Skip. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail.

nodes.name: Send Onboarding Stage Email
nodes.notes:
Sends the compliance-approved onboarding email to the client. Uses message_out from the guardrail, which carries the required unsubscribe footer — plain text only, since the footer is only guaranteed to be present in the text version the guardrail returns. Subject is read from 'Build Onboarding Stage Email' since the guardrail doesn't touch subjects.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: Skip Client Opt-Out
nodes.notes: This client has opted out of firm emails. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail workflow. No email is sent.

main.node: Fetch Firm Users from Clio API
Filter Matters with Email and Date
Filter Matters Due for Stage Today
Fetch Open Matters from Clio API
Check If Stages Are Due Today

description: Fires daily, fetches the firm's user directory from Clio, then every open matter. Splits, filters, and stages each matter with native n8n nodes, computing purely from each matter's own open date whether today is one of four onboarding-sequence days: Day 0 (portal access), Day 1 (what to expect), Day 3 (document checklist), Day 7 (first-bill explainer). The matching email is personalized with the assigned attorney's name where resolvable, checked against the Bar-Compliance Guardrail for opt-out and disclaimer, then sent if approved. Skips silently on days with nothing due. Replaces a Lawmatics-style onboarding journey — a rocky first week is one of the top drivers of early client churn.
